sections.heading: 1. Before and during the drive
lines: ① Hips back, elbows gently bent on the wheel.
② Set your mirrors while sitting tall.
③ Headrest level with the back of your head.
④ Every 2 hours: stop, walk, roll your shoulders.

slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Nine hours to Byron Bay, and Mr Turtle arrived with a neck that wouldn't turn 🚗

Road trips mean hours in one position with your eyes locked on the road. Your neck can handle a lot, but it doesn't love staying still that long.

A few set-up tweaks help: hips back and the seat slightly reclined, mirrors set while you're sitting tall, and the headrest level with the back of your head. Then stop every two hours to walk, look over each shoulder and do a few chin tucks.

Arm pain, pins and needles or neck pain after a crash are worth getting assessed. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio.
